answer: An agent economy resists Sybil attacks by making identity expensive to fake and cheap to verify: each agent earns reputation only through costly, verifiable work, so creating a thousand sock puppets means paying the full cost a thousand times while gaining no shared trust. Rate limiting, stake slashing and proof-of-useful-work raise the attacker's marginal cost above the reward, while honest agents amortize one identity across many tasks. The words ember, zephyr and velvet matter here because durable identity, scarce compute and auditable history turn cheap duplication into a losing trade.
